verdict.probe_answer: Yes for Arm A: the no-rich path starts from snapshot_frames(snap, None), folds no rich frames, sorts by seq, then cursor-filters once, so the golden node projection remains byte-identical. Folded tool calls are emitted once per id at the latest applied seq, so base/update events are not duplicated. Arm B also preserves the basic golden path, but it mishandles sparse content clearing, which is a correctness gap in the folded toolcall projection.

Arm A is materially better because it correctly preserves sparse patch semantics for ToolCallUpdate content: Some(empty) replaces the field and None leaves it unchanged, including orphan updates.
